entries.title: Alto Adige: cenni geografici e statistici
text: A geographical and statistical outline of Alto Adige by A. R. Toniolo, published by De Agostini in 1919. One of two period books found online that present the new province to Italian readers. The celebratory municipal and party volumes of the fascist years were not found.
facts: A. R. Toniolo, Alto Adige: cenni geografici e statistici, Novara, Istituto Geografico De Agostini, 1919; scan from the University of Illinois on the Internet Archive (manifest)

Listed among the period books 'presenting the province to Italians' on the Internet Archive; with Borgese 1921 one of the two most relevant, and downloaded because out of copyright (notes 03, §4, [V])
The celebratory municipal and party volumes ('Bolzano fascista', decennial volumes, industrial-zone brochures) were not found online; these two books were (notes 03, §4)
Rights: author died 1955, so public domain in Italy since 1 January 2026; published before 1929, so also public domain in the USA (manifest)

entries.title: L'Alto Adige contro l'Italia: quattro lettere da Bolzano con aggiunti quattro programmi di Alto Adige autonomo
text: G. A. Borgese, “Alto Adige against Italy”: four letters from Bolzano, followed by four programmes for an autonomous Alto Adige, published in Milan in 1921. The second of the two period books found online that present the province to Italians. It is known here by its title only and has not been read.

entries.title: Alpenzeitung, 13 July 1926, page 1
text: Front page: “S. M. König Viktor Emanuel III. in Bolzano.” The King lays the first stone of the Monument to Victory, sprinkled, the paper says, with water from the Piave. La Stampa ran “L'Alto Adige acclama al Re” on its own front page the same day.
facts: Front page (of 6): King Victor Emmanuel III in Bolzano; foundation stone of the Victory Monument (manifest)

entries.title: Dolomiten, 9 July 1928, page 1
text: The Catholic German-language Dolomiten announces “Hohe Gäste bei der Enthüllung des Siegesdenkmals in Bolzano”. The paper appeared three times a week, sold about 30,000 copies and was heavily censored.

entries.title: La Provincia di Bolzano, 13 July 1928, page 1
text: The Italian daily of the Fascist federation on the same day: “IL GRANDIOSO RITO DI IERI IN BOLZANO FASCISTA. Il Sovrano consacra nel Monumento alla Vittoria il segno antico e nuovo del diritto immortale d'Italia.”
Masthead, headlines and text are all in roman type. Set beside the Alpenzeitung of that week, the two languages of the city are also two typefaces.
facts: Front page (4 pages in the issue). Headline 'IL GRANDIOSO RITO DI IERI IN BOLZANO FASCISTA - Il Sovrano consacra nel Monumento alla Vittoria il segno antico e nuovo del diritto immortale d'Italia'; masthead: Quotidiano della Federazione Provinciale Fascista (manifest)
Also on the page: 'Il discorso di Giuriati' (notes 03, §1D, [V-img])
Same event elsewhere: La Stampa 'LA CONSACRAZIONE EROICA DI BOLZANO ITALIANA'; Dolomiten's appeasing line to 'abroad'; the AZ on German radio's coverage (notes 03, §1E)

Seen in the image: masthead, headlines and body text all in roman type, no blackletter; columns include 'Dopo la celebrazione', 'La memorabile giornata', 'Il duplice monumento' and 'L'arrivo di S. M. il Re'

entries.title: Alpenzeitung, 29 October 1931, page 3
text: “Die Feier des 9. Jahrestages der fascistischen Revolution in Bolzano.” The day after the anniversary the paper lists what was opened: Ponte Druso, the municipal baths, the health-insurance building, a radio transmitter, a power station, a barracks, a tram line. At nine in the morning Prefect Marziali cut the ribbon on the bridge.

A column headed “Werke des Regimes” gives the bridge's measurements and cost and describes the eagles on globes on fasces. The page is set in Fraktur. The pictures are the scan and five captures taken by hand from the library's viewer.
facts: Page 3 (of 8): 'Eröffnung von Bauwerken des Regimes: Drususbrücke ...' (the 28 Oct. 1931 inaugurations) (manifest); the Europeana OCR is garbled (notes 03, §1C, item 11)

Headline: 'Die Feier des 9. Jahrestages der fascistischen Revolution in Bolzano. Eröffnung von Bauwerken des Regimes: Drususbrücke, städt. Badeanstalt, Palast der Krankenkasse, Rundfunksender der „Eiar", Elektrizitätswerk in Val d'Ega, Artilleriekaserne in Oltrisarco, Tramlinie von Vurza nach Laives usw. - Aushebung der Jungen Italienerinnen' (notes 07, §1, [T])

At 9 a.m. Prefect Marziali was received at the Drususbrücke 'vom Erbauer Ing. Cav. Albini und dem technischen Stab'; a scissor cut, the tricolour ribbon fell and the bridge was handed to traffic (notes 07, §1, [T])

'Werke des Regimes - Die Drususbrücke': 102.30 m long, three arches (middle span 34.70 m), reinforced concrete faced in porphyry; cost 3,000,000 lire, 800,000 of it from the Comune; works began 9 January 1930 (notes 07, §1, [T])

The corner piers carry helmets with a Roman shield and swords that 'mark the beginning and the end of the war'; the columns with the Roman eagles rest on globes carried by the lictor's bundle. The notes read this as settling 'Roman or fascist': both, by design (notes 07, §1, [T])
Doubt: the builder 'Albini' is not among the engineers (Miozzi, Ricci) named by the secondary sources of thread 05; perhaps the site or contractor's engineer [INF] (notes 07, §1)

Seen in the image: the banner headline is set in a condensed bold roman (sans-serif) type and the long subhead in roman, while the body text and the side heading 'Werke des Regimes' are in Fraktur; the five further pictures are hand captures of the same page in the Teßmann viewer (manifest 07)

entries.title: Alpenzeitung, 21 February 1935, page 1
text: “Mussolini für die Schaffung von Groß-Bolzano.” The Duce orders the industrial zone. The Italian daily's headline that day was “Il Duce per la più grande Bolzano”: the German is a word-for-word calque, which fits the claim that the Alpenzeitung largely translated its Italian sister paper.
One story, one publisher, two languages, two typefaces.
facts: Front page (of 6): 'Mussolini für die Schaffung von Groß-Bolzano - Der Duce verfügt in einer bedeutsamen Sitzung über die Errichtung der Industriezone' (manifest; notes 03, §1C, item 13, [V])

The same story under three headlines: LPB 'Il Duce per la più grande Bolzano', AZ 'Mussolini für die Schaffung von Groß-Bolzano', La Stampa 'Una zona industriale a Bolzano sorgerà per volontà del Duce' (notes 03, §1E, [V-img][V])

The calque 'più grande Bolzano' → 'Groß-Bolzano' fits the claim that the AZ was largely German translations of LPB articles from the same publisher [I]; that claim rests on a Wikipedia mirror only [U] (notes 03, §1F)
Seen in the image: blackletter masthead 'Alpenzeitung', 'Politisches Tagblatt der Provinz Bolzano', 'Donnerstag, den 21. Februar 1935-XIII', '10. Jahrgang'; banner headline and body text in Fraktur

entries.title: La Provincia di Bolzano, 21 February 1935, page 1
text: “Le direttive del Capo per l'immediata realizzazione della zona industriale. Il Duce per la più grande Bolzano.” The communiqué names the industrialists: Falck, Donegani, Lancia, Rivetti, Goisis. A kicker in condensed capitals and a bold serif banner stand over roman text. The copy scanned carries the stamp of the municipal library of Trento.
facts: Front page (6 pages in the issue). Headline 'LE DIRETTIVE DEL CAPO PER L'IMMEDIATA REALIZZAZIONE DELLA ZONA INDUSTRIALE - Il Duce per la più grande Bolzano'; the communiqué names Falck, Donegani, Lancia, Rivetti and Goisis; masthead: Quotidiano del Partito Nazionale Fascista (manifest)
The subhead lists the chemical, automobile, steel and clothing industries (notes 03, §1D, [V-img])

The same story under three headlines: LPB 'Il Duce per la più grande Bolzano', AZ 'Mussolini für die Schaffung von Groß-Bolzano', La Stampa 'Una zona industriale a Bolzano sorgerà per volontà del Duce' (notes 03, §1E)

entries.title: La Provincia di Bolzano, 26 October 1939, page 1
text: “L'applicazione degli accordi italo-tedeschi. Le norme per il rimpatrio dei cittadini germanici e per l'emigrazione di allogeni tedeschi dall'Alto Adige in Germania.”
For Italian readers the Option is a repatriation and an emigration of “allogeni”, people of another stock. The German-language papers called the same text an option of citizenship.
facts: Front page (6 pages in the issue). Headline 'L'APPLICAZIONE DEGLI ACCORDI ITALO-TEDESCHI - Le norme per il rimpatrio dei cittadini germanici e per l'emigrazione di allogeni tedeschi dall'Alto Adige in Germania', then 'Il testo delle norme' (manifest)
Signed 'Giuseppe Mastromattei, Prefetto di Bolzano - Otto Bene, Console Generale di Germania a Milano' (notes 03, §1D, [V-img])

LPB addresses Italian readers ('allogeni', 'rimpatrio'), AZ and DOL German speakers ('Option', 'Umsiedlung') [I] (notes 03, §1E)

Seen in the image: kicker and two-line banner in condensed sans-serif; a boxed preamble signed by Mastromattei and Bene; then 'Il testo delle „norme"' in small roman type across the page, section 'Disposizioni relative alle persone'; a Biblioteca Comunale Trento stamp over the masthead

entries.title: Dolomiten, 27 October 1939, page 5
text: The Dolomiten prints the same rules as “Ausführungsbestimmungen für die Option der Staatsbürgerschaft”, with the two forms: white to keep Italian citizenship, yellow-red for German citizenship and emigration. The picture and the text held look like two different pages of the same article.
facts: Page 5 (of 11): Dolomiten prints the same Option implementing rules (manifest)
'Ausführungsbestimmungen für die Option der Staatsbürgerschaft' (same text, in Dolomiten) (notes 03, §1C, item 23, [V])
One text, three framings: LPB's 'rimpatrio' and 'allogeni' against the AZ and DOL 'Option der Staatsbürgerschaft' (notes 03, §1E)

Seen in the image: no page number visible; the scan shows the opening of the text, 'Richtlinien für die Rückwanderung der Reichsdeutschen und Abwanderung der Volksdeutschen aus dem Alto Adige in das Deutsche Reich', a 'Gemeinsames Vorwort' signed by Giuseppe Mastromattei, Präfekt von Bolzano, and Otto Bene, Deutscher Generalkonsul in Mailand, and 'Erster Abschnitt: Bestimmungen über die Personen' (§§ 1-17); set in Fraktur throughout

entries.title: Alpenzeitung, 23 November 1939, page 5
text: A boxed notice that the paper ran nine times in a month: “Die Option der Atesiner”. Whoever keeps Italian citizenship “und dadurch beweist, daß er sich als Italiener fühlt ... wird in seiner Heimat bleiben können”. To stay was to feel Italian.
facts: Page 5 (of 6): recurring box 'Die Option der Atesiner' - staying means 'feeling Italian' (manifest)

'Die Option der Atesiner: Wer sich für die Beibehaltung der italienischen Staatsbürgerschaft entschließt und dadurch beweist, daß er sich als Italiener fühlt ... wird in seiner Heimat bleiben können' (notes 03, §1C, item 26, [V])
The AZ ran the box on 23.11, 26.11, 01.12, 12.12, 13.12, 14.12, 15.12, 17.12 and 21.12.1939, equating staying with feeling Italian (notes 03, §1E, [V])
The box cites 'Art. 2 der „Erläuterungen zum italienisch-deutschen Abkommen"' (OCR)
Seen in the image: page head 'Aus Bolzano Stadt und Land' in large blackletter; the small boxed item 'Die Option der Atesiner' sits in the middle column; Fraktur throughout

entries.title: La Provincia di Bolzano, 11 January 1940, page 1
text: “I risultati ufficiali delle opzioni in Alto Adige comunicati al Duce e al Führer.” For the province of Bolzano: 166,488 for German citizenship, 27,712 for Italian, 35,300 with no declaration.
The box stands at the top right of a front page led by the war in Finland. La Stampa ran the identical headline the same day.
facts: Front page (6 pages in the issue). Headline 'I RISULTATI UFFICIALI delle opzioni in Alto Adige comunicati al Duce e al Führer': province of Bolzano 166.488 for German citizenship, 27.712 for Italian, 35.300 no declaration; masthead: Quotidiano fascista dell'Alto Adige (manifest)
For the Trento mixed-language zone: 24,453 eligible; 13,015 for Germany, 3,802 for Italy, 7,636 no declaration (notes 03, §1D, [V-img])
La Stampa carries the identical headline the same day; one Stefani/ministry text syndicated to all three papers [I] (notes 03, §1E)

Seen in the image: the results box stands at top right; the lead story is the Finnish counter-offensive ('La vittoriosa controffensiva finlandese si sviluppa in territorio sovietico'); set in roman type with condensed sans-serif headlines

Rights: out of copyright as a collective, unsigned issue (l. 633/1941, art. 26-27), but the gallery states no terms of use: treat as a study copy and ask the library before any publication; the Codice dei beni culturali (art. 108) may also apply (manifest)
